text:
ting: Quick sync — I brought up artemis-13b on int6 and int4 overnight. Ran a small live-slice (1k samples) against our GTN prompts. TL;DR: int6 looks like the best cost/quality sweet spot for product, int4 is cheap but has noticeable regressions on stop-sequence and hallucination-sensitive prompts.

jess: Awesome, can you paste the micro scorecard and the config you used?

ting: Sure — configs:
- fp16 baseline (v2026.03.19)
- int6 quant (QAT-ish pipeline, per-tensor tweak)
- int4 quant (aggressive, per-channel fallback on attention)

Here's the quick table from the run:```
Model | config | p95 latency | qps (avg) | tokens_per_$ | qual_delta (vs fp16)
Artemis-13b | fp16 | 120ms | 105 | 1.0e6 | baseline
Artemis-13b | int6 | 135ms | 98 | 1.45e6 | -0.6% (EM/perf)
Artemis-13b | int4 | 190ms | 68 | 2.1e6 | -2.9% (same prompts)
```
Notes: p95 measured on our canary fleet (4x A100 equiv). tokens_per_$ is estimate from observed throughput and per-token kernel cost.

sam: Nice numbers. Where are the error modes concentrated? Is the int6 suffering from specific categories?

ting: int6 regressions are mostly: tighter stop-sequence failures (1.2% -> 1.8%), short factual hallucinations on named entities (tiny bump), and occasional tokenization edge-case wording shifts. int4 has broader degradation on multi-step reasoning prompts and a clear drop in rerank quality.

ivan: infra note — int4 memory wins are great but KV cache access pattern increases CPU overhead on our runtime; that explains the latency p95 jump. Need to check kernel scheduling.

maya: For GTN routing: product wants max cost reduction without hurting core flows. My read: promote int6 to 60-70% of traffic for non-critical flows (search snippets, short completions) and keep fp16 for heavy multi-turn and billing-sensitive features. Agree?

jess: I agree with that split. Also recommend a 5% holdback to fp16 for quality monitoring + a 1% randomized sample to int4 for continued econ signal only (not user-facing).

roman: +1, and add a canary tag in rollout: route by prompt signature hash (we already have hooks). We'll need a fallback policy: if int6 quality delta > 1% for a given slice, fallback to fp16 automatically.

deploy-bot: deploy: artemis-13b-int6 v2026.03.20 promoted to canary pool (tag: artemis-int6-canary).

ting: Proposed action items:
1) Sam/maya: approve traffic split (proposed: int6 65%, fp16 30%, int4 5% econ-only) — want GTN signoff.
2) Ivan/infra: investigate int4 kernel latency spike and see if batching tweaks help; estimate due EOD tomorrow.
3) Jess/QA: create holdback monitors (stop-sequence, named-entity recall, rerank precision) and wire rollback triggers (1% absolute drop on any primary metric).
4) Roman: implement prompt-signature routing + automatic fallback for slices where delta > threshold.

sam: I can approve the split for an initial 48h pilot, as long as the holdback monitors are in place.

maya: approved for pilot. Please keep product alerted if we see UX regressions.

ting: I'll open the small notebook + perf logs here: https://redwood.internal/notebooks/artemis-int6-econ (private) and drop a short summary doc later. If folks want raw outputs, ping me — I can paste a few failing examples for int4.

jess: Pls add the 5% fp16 holdback to the rollout config and tag metrics with rollout_id. Also add a human override for rollback.

ivan: Working on a quick scheduling shim — will post perf run once done.

ting: Thanks all. If we survive 48h without regression, we’ll propose moving int6 to 75% traffic and keep int4 as a shadow econ-scan. :thumbsup:

roman: I'll add the fallback rule and make the routing config editable in console.

maya: Good plan. Keep GTN folks in the loop.

ting: End of thread — will follow up with notebook + short signal table tomorrow morning.
